Brothers - Daedalus - Elphinstone::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Days 2-7: Departure in the morning. Boat, diving, safety, and Scientific equipment briefing. Onboard briefing. Orientation dives. The Brother Islands are one of the best diving spots in the world. The Islands – the Big Brother and the Little Brother– are two small isolated promontories that just come out of the water in the middle of the sea at some 60 km from the coast. The Little Brother has a very high concentration of life in a very reduced area. The walls are covered literally with sponges, anemones, and all sorts of soft coral alcyonarian in an astonishing variety of colors and shapes. Of course, you will find here plenty of fish. It is not unusual to see sharks: hammerheads, thresher sharks, grey sharks, silvertip, and white-tip reef sharks. About one km north of the Little Brother lies the Big Brother. Situated, in the middle of the island, is a lighthouse. When it is not too windy, you can proceed to dive into the wreck “Numidia” which lies upon the reef on the northern side of the island between 10 and 80 m. This 150 m long ship sunk 100 years ago and is now completely covered with both hard and soft corals and gorgonias. A fantastic view! On the NW side of the island, you will find another wreck: the “AIDA“. This 82 m long steam ship sunk in 1957. The remaining pieces of the wreck are scattered all over the reef and just a small section of the hull can be found between 30 and 60 m. It is nicely overgrown and worth visiting. Because of strong currents and possibly high waves, it is not easy to dive at the Brothers. This safari is only for experienced divers. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

Deep South, St. Johns::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Days 2-7: Departure in the morning. Boat, diving, safety, and Scientific equipment briefing. Deep, deep in the south - near Rocky Island - are the St. John’s Reefs. You will find their exciting drop-offs. The wall of one of the reefs is overgrown with big gorgonians, and the wall of the other reef is overgrown with all kinds of colorful soft corals. You will find a lot of fish, and in the blue, you can see with a little bit of luck “big fish” like Hammerheads, Grey sharks, Silvertip, White Tip Reef Sharks, Barracudas, Tunas, and Mackerels. Sometimes even you can see Mantas and dolphins. It is possible to reach St. John’s Reefs in one week, but you are going to sail a lot (mostly at night) and the time is very short to dive at all the reefs in St. John’s. Because of the long distance, some groups decide to do a 10 or 13 day safari cruise in combination with Abu Fendera. Abu Fendera Reef. The main reef is around 6 km long and full of hard coral. In front of this reef, you can see some parts like a small reef or ergs, which are 400 - 800 meters. You can go diving between the reefs. So, you can plan and make a lot of different dives there. In front of the reefs, you will see a lot of ergs. And there are the most beautiful soft corals. Also, you can see a lot of fish. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

North Classic::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Days 2-7: Departure in the morning. Boat, diving, safety and Scientific equipment briefing. Onboard briefing. Orientation dives. The SS Thistlegorm wreck dive site. The Thistlegorm is the best-known and most popular wreck dive in the Red Sea. It lies on the west coast of the Sinai Peninsula and 40 km from Sharm El Sheikh, The Thistlegorm sank after just 18 months after her launch in April 1940. It was carrying military equipment during World War II, such as Morris cars, Bedford Trucks, motorcycles, spare tank and aircraft parts, grenades, guns, munitions, mines, artillery, and much more that made it one of the best diving sites in the Red Sea. In the early hours of the 6th of October 1941, the Thistlegorm was split in 2 and sank almost instantly after being hit by "2" bombs from a German long-range bomber. The Thistlegorm wreck is one of the best diving sites in the Red Sea. In fact, one of the best diving sites in the world. The Dunraven wreck diving. The Dunraven, a steam and sail-powered vessel used to transport spices and timber, ran aground the reef Shaab Machmud in March 1876 during a voyage from Bombay to Newcastle and sank quickly. The ship broke in two, and her two halves came to rest on the sea floor. The wreck lies upside down with the stern at a depth of 28 m and the bow at 18 m. At the stern, you find the propeller and the rudder, which are overgrown with corals. Inside the wreck, you see thousands of glassfish Shark and Yolanda reef dive site. You will also enjoy another more than wonderful scuba diving experience in Sharks and Yolanda reef, which is rated as one of the top ten dive sites, not just in the Red Sea but in the world, with wonderful marine life, where the coral reefs are a colorful and great variety. Divers flock to Yolanda reef to explore the remains of the Yolanda, an old Cypriot cargo ship that ran aground in 1980. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. North Wrecks::7.programme:

Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Days 2-7: Departure in the morning. The best wreck diving safari in the Northern Red Sea. The North Wrecks is the ultimate Red Sea liveaboard route for wreck divers. Six historic shipwrecks spanning from 1941 WWII cargo ships to a 1991 passenger ferry - every dive day includes a wreck, and most include a night dive to experience the same hull in a completely different light. The route runs north from Hurghada through the Safaga offshore reefs (Salem Express, Middle Reef, Panorama), then into the Strait of Gubal where the most legendary wrecks of the Red Sea cluster: SS Thistlegorm, Giannis D at Sha’ab Abu Nuhas, Rosalie Moller, and the Gubal Island sites. All levels of wreck diver welcome - from the relatively shallow Giannis D (4–27m) to the deep technical territory of the Rosalie Moller (mast at 17m, deck at 35–40m). Night dives on this route are exceptional: the Thistlegorm becomes an eerie, torch-lit time capsule; Middle Reef transforms with hunting cephalopods; Tobi Arba’a’s pinnacles come alive with Spanish dancers and decorator crabs; and The Barge at Gubal Island is considered one of the finest night dives in the northern Red Sea. SS Thistlegorm - world’s most famous WWII wreck - dawn + night dive from liveaboard. Giannis D - most accessible wreck at Sha’ab Abu Nuhas - 4–27m. Salem Express - Egyptian passenger ferry 1991 - emotional, powerful dive. Rosalie Moller - WWII sister ship of Thistlegorm - sunk 48 hrs later, intact at 35–50m. 5 night dives - Middle Reef, Tobi Arba’a x2, Thistlegorm, The Barge at Gubal. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

North & Easy::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: Shaab El Erg for a check dive. Day 3: Dive 1 on either Shark and Yolanda or Shark Observatory, dive 2 either the canyon inside Marsa Bareika or Zatar or Ghozlani. Providing the weather is calm and with no wind, the boat heads straight to Gordon Reef (Tiran) for our first 'open deck' opportunity for either a 3rd dive and a night (or dusk) dive. If the weather is windy, dive at Temple instead for ‘open deck’, 3rd and night (dusk) dive. Day 4: 'Open deck' dive from the boat at Gordon Reef, or a ride on the rib to Thomas Reef for a dive there. Later the boat moves to Jackson for either one or two dives there, or one dive there and then a dive at either Ras Nasrani or Tower before mooring for the night at Temple for the night dive, or instead go straight to Dunraven and night dive on a nearby reef. Day 5: Early departure to Dunraven for dive 1 and dive 2 on the Thistlegorm (or vice versa). Cross to Gubal and moor over the Barge, or 3rd dive at Thistlegorm and leave for Gubal for a dusk or night dive. Day 6: 'Open deck' on the Barge, plus 1 or 2 dives on the Ulysses (weather permitting). Alternatively, guests can opt to choose 4 between 5:30 and 18:30. Option to dive from the rib at Gubal Reef or at Bluff Point (subject to conditions). Day 7: 'Open deck' until 10:00 with the 3rd dive at Shaab El Erg to end the week where we began. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

On our last day in Tubbataha we depart for a sunset cruise to Cagayancillo to the amazing Calusa island. Day 7: After overnight cruise we arrive in the island of Calusa for our secret dive spot where we can find hammer heads and big schools of fish along with spectacular coral reef. Then we cruise into the shallow reef and anchor. Guests can go on the white sand beach of a private island before having the final dive. Deep South Red Sea Expedition::12.programme:
Program
Day 1: ARRIVAL IN MARSA ALAM – HAMATA Arrival by flight at Marsa Alam International Airport (RMF). Guests will be transferred from Marsa Alam Airport to Hamata, with a transfer time of approximately 2 hours. Upon arrival: - Check-in on board NEW LIFE - Welcome and introduction to the crew and professional dive guides - Safety briefing - Equipment preparation - Dinner on board - Overnight on board in Hamata Day 2: CHECK DIVES – FURY SHOAL The expedition begins with check dives in the spectacular Fury Shoal area. Shaab Claudio An easy and beautiful orientation dive through an impressive cave and swim-through system. This is the perfect opportunity to become familiar with the diving conditions and explore the spectacular underwater formations. Sataya Reef – South / Dolphin House A spectacular reef area famous for encounters with spinner dolphins. Sightings are very likely and can provide an unforgettable wildlife experience. Afternoon Departure – St. John’s In the afternoon, NEW LIFE departs towards St. John’s Reefs. Approximate crossing time: 7 hours, depending on sea and weather conditions. Day 3-11: ST. JOHN’S REEFS Habili Ali A spectacular open-water wall dive with the possibility of encountering reef sharks. The steep wall drops into the deep blue and offers an impressive Red Sea diving experience. Gota Kebira A huge coral formation and an ideal location for a drift dive along the reef wall, with impressive coral formations and abundant marine life. A further dive at Gota Kebira may be scheduled depending on the conditions and the daily dive plan. Departure – Abu Fendera After the diving program, NEW LIFE departs towards Abu Fendera. Approximate crossing time: 7 hours. Day 4: ABU FENDERA – THE GATEWAY TO PRISTINE REEFS Today we explore the remote and largely untouched reef systems of Abu Fendera. Abu Fendera North A very remote reef system featuring impressive giant pillar corals and pristine underwater landscapes. Abu Fendera East A spectacular drift dive along untouched reef areas with beautiful macro life and soft corals. Abu Fendera West A shallower and more relaxed dive, allowing guests to enjoy the reef and marine life at a comfortable pace. Departure – Elba Reef After the final dive, NEW LIFE departs towards Elba Reef. Approximate crossing time: 7 hours. Day 5: ELBA REEF – INTO THE REMOTE SOUTH Arrival at the remote Elba Reef, one of the most pristine and untouched diving areas of the Red Sea. Up to three dives at spectacular steep walls and colourful coral reefs, with excellent opportunities to encounter sharks, eagle rays, barracuda and large schools of fish. The remote location and limited diver traffic make Elba Reef one of the true highlights of the expedition. Day 6: ELBA REEF – EXPLORING PRISTINE REEFS Continue exploring the unique reef system of Elba Reef with up to three dives at varied steep walls, coral gardens and reef plateaus. Crystal-clear water, healthy coral formations and exceptional marine biodiversity make Elba Reef one of the absolute highlights of this expedition. Day 7: ELBA REEF – FINAL DIVES & DEPARTURE FOR ST. JOHN’S Enjoy the final dives around Elba Reef, depending on weather, sea conditions and the planned itinerary. Early Afternoon – Departure for St. John’s In the early afternoon, NEW LIFE departs Elba Reef and heads towards St. John’s Reefs. Approximate crossing time: 14 hours, depending on sea and weather conditions. Overnight sailing towards the spectacular reefs of St. John’s. Day 8: ST. JOHN’S & ST. JOHN’S CAVES Arrival in the St. John’s area and a full day of diving. Explore spectacular reef formations, walls, caves and underwater passages in this remote southern Red Sea region. St. John’s Caves A highlight of the area, featuring impressive caves, tunnels and swim-throughs combined with colourful coral formations and rich marine life. The exact dive sites and number of dives will depend on local conditions and the final itinerary. Day 9: SATAYA – GOTTA SORAYA; GOTTA KEBIR – SHILINIAT The expedition continues towards Sataya and the surrounding reef systems. Gotta Soraya & Gotta Kebir Explore spectacular reef formations with impressive coral structures, walls and abundant marine life. Shiliniat Continue exploring the reef system of Shiliniat, depending on the prevailing conditions and the dive plan for the day. Day 10: SHAAB MARSA ALAM – ELPHINSTONE – ABU DABAB The expedition continues north with a diverse selection of renowned dive locations. Shaab Marsa Alam Explore the reef formations and marine life of Shaab Marsa Alam. Elphinstone Reef One of the most famous reefs in the Egyptian Red Sea, offering spectacular walls, colourful coral formations and opportunities for encounters with larger pelagic marine life. Abu Dabab A well-known reef area offering varied diving and the opportunity to explore its rich marine environment. Day 11: MARSA SHONA – MARSA TROMBI – MANGROVE BAY Continue north with a full day of diving along the Red Sea coast. Marsa Shona Explore the reef and diverse marine life of Marsa Shona. Marsa Trombi Continue to Marsa Trombi for another dive and discover its reef formations and marine environment. Mangrove Bay A relaxed and scenic diving experience surrounded by the characteristic coastal landscape. The exact number and timing of dives depend on the conditions and the final itinerary. Day 12: SALEM EXPRESS – RETURN TO PORT Today features a dive at the legendary Salem Express, one of the best-known wrecks in the Egyptian Red Sea. After the diving program, NEW LIFE returns to the port at approximately 13:00. The afternoon is at leisure: - Relax and enjoy the facilities on board - Free time to explore the surrounding area - Prepare equipment and luggage - Final evening aboard NEW LIFE Day 13 : CHECK-OUT & DEPARTURE After breakfast, guests check out from NEW LIFE. A transfer to the airport will then be arranged for the guests' individual journey home. The itinerary is designed as an expedition and may be adjusted according to weather, wind, sea conditions, tides, local regulations, port requirements and operational considerations. The exact sequence of dive sites and number of dives may therefore change. The final itinerary is determined by the Captain and professional dive guides, always with safety as the highest priority. The remote southern itinerary includes destinations such as Elba Reef, Abu Fendera and St. John's, making this an exceptional expedition for experienced divers seeking pristine reefs, spectacular walls, abundant marine life and remote Red Sea diving.

Deep South Red Sea Expedition::14.programme:
Program
Day 1 – 24 July ARRIVAL IN HURGHADA – CHECK-IN ON BOARD Guests arrive in Hurghada and check in on board NEW LIFE. - Check-in and cabin allocation - Welcome on board - Meet the crew and professional dive guides - Safety briefing - Equipment preparation - Dinner on board - Overnight on board in Hurghada Marina Day 2 – 25 July DEPARTURE – HURGHADA → BROTHERS ISLANDS After breakfast, NEW LIFE departs Hurghada and begins the journey towards the legendary Brothers Islands. The crossing takes approximately 8 hours, depending on sea and weather conditions. Once at the destination, the diving program begins according to the conditions and the itinerary. BROTHERS ISLANDS Famous for dramatic walls, strong currents, colorful soft corals and frequent encounters with oceanic whitetip sharks, hammerhead sharks, grey reef sharks and thresher sharks. The Brothers are also home to the legendary wrecks Aida II and Numidia. DAEDALUS REEF An isolated offshore reef known for spectacular drop-offs, pristine coral formations and excellent opportunities to encounter hammerhead sharks, oceanic whitetips and large pelagic species. ROCKY ISLAND One of the most remote and untouched dive sites in the Red Sea. Steep walls covered with colourful soft corals attract tuna, barracuda, grey reef sharks and other pelagic fish. ZABARGAD ISLAND A beautiful island surrounded by crystal-clear waters, coral gardens, caves and steep reef walls. Frequent encounters include turtles, Napoleon wrasse and reef sharks. ST. JOHN'S REEFS A vast reef system in the far south featuring tunnels, caverns, pinnacles, drop-offs and coral gardens. St. John's is known for its exceptional biodiversity and spectacular underwater landscapes. ELBA REEF Located close to the Egyptian-Sudanese border, Elba offers pristine reefs with minimal diver traffic, healthy coral formations and abundant marine life in an untouched environment. ABU FENDERA A remote plateau reef famous for impressive hard coral formations, large schools of fish and excellent visibility. One of the hidden gems of the Southern Red Sea. FURY SHOAL A collection of spectacular reefs featuring caves, swim-throughs, coral gardens and sheltered lagoons. Highlights include Shaab Claudio, Shaab Maksour and Malahi, often referred to as the “Underwater Labyrinth.” MARINE LIFE Oceanic Whitetip Sharks • Hammerhead Sharks • Grey Reef Sharks • Silvertip Sharks • Thresher Sharks • Turtles • Dolphins • Napoleon Wrasse • Barracuda • Tuna • Giant Trevallies • Eagle Rays • Schools of Anthias and Fusiliers Day 13 – 06 August FINAL DIVES & ARRIVAL IN HAMATA The final morning offers the opportunity for the last dives of the expedition. After the final dives and lunch, NEW LIFE sails towards Hamata. Afternoon – Arrival in Hamata - Arrival in Hamata - Final equipment preparation and packing - Relaxing afternoon on board - Farewell dinner - Last night on board in Hamata Day 14 – 07 August DEPARTURE – HAMATA → HURGHADA After breakfast, it is time to say goodbye to NEW LIFE and the crew. - Breakfast on board - Check-out and disembarkation - Group transfer from Hamata to Hurghada - Estimated transfer time: approximately 5–6 hours End of the Deep South Red Sea Expedition. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Total Solar Eclipse Expedition - Elphins.programme:
Program
Day 1: Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. A once-in-a-century event, in the middle of the sea On Monday 2 August 2027, the moon's shadow will sweep across Upper Egypt and out over the Red Sea, delivering the second-longest total solar eclipse of the 21st century — and the longest anyone alive today will ever see from this region again. While hundreds of thousands crowd into Luxor, our guests will experience totality from the one place no land observer can reach: the open sea, positioned precisely on the eclipse centerline. For more than six minutes, day becomes night. The temperature drops, stars appear at midday, and the sun's corona blazes above a darkened sea. From the deck you'll watch the moon's shadow race toward you across the water and a 360-degree sunset glow ring the entire horizon — a spectacle only visible from a ship. This is not an eclipse cruise with diving attached. It is a world-class dive safari that happens to sit beneath a once-in-a-century sky. Sinai Classic::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2-7: Morning: sail to nearby Temple or Ras Katy for a check dive. The week-long safari will cover the area from the Strait of Tiran, Ras Mohamed National Park and the Gulf of Suez which is usually visited first. The National Park begins at the small bay of Marsa Ghazlani followed by the larger and deeper bay of Marsa Bareika. Continuing along the coast to Ras Za’atar, Jackfish Alley, Eel Garden, and Shark Observatory, to the southern end of the peninsula with Anemone City, Shark Reef, and Yolanda Reef and ending at the Quay. Because of the geographic position, this is a privileged area distinguished to strong massive currents that transport large quantities of plankton and other food that give rise to an extraordinary growth of stony and soft corals and attract large schools of both reef and pelagic marine fauna, over a thousand species in all. Schooling barracuda, jackfish, tuna and many kinds of sharks swim in these deep blue waters, especially in summer from June to August, sometimes early September. The safari will also take you to famous sites like the wrecks of Dunraven and Thistlegorm, Shag Rock and the wreck of Kingston, sail to Sha’ab Ali where pods of dolphins are common, explore several spots at Sha’ab Mahmouds reef system. Don’t miss the four famous reefs in the Strait of Tiran: Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse and Gordon Reef, probably the most interesting and richest in marine life. You can choose from several dive sites with superb wall and drift diving. In the afternoon of the 7th day, the boat will return to the Sharm area. Day 7-8: Depending on your check out and flight time return to New Marina (El Wataneya) port and disembark. Transfer to airport or hotel. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

Best of Dahab and Tiran::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Arrival and Embarkation (Hurghada) Guests are greeted at the Hurghada airport and transferred to the liveaboard. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome drink and a refreshing towel, followed by an introduction to the crew and a safety briefing. Guests settle into their cabins, followed by equipment checks with assistance from the dive team. Spend the evening relaxing, enjoying a delicious dinner onboard, and getting ready for the adventure ahead. Days 2 to 5: Diving Dahab and Tiran Over these four days, guests will explore the underwater treasures of Dahab and Tiran. Dive highlights may include: Dahab's Blue Hole: A world-famous dive site with dramatic walls and a deep, azure blue drop-off. Canyon Reef: Known for its mesmerizing caverns and swim-throughs, teeming with marine life. Tiran's Jackson Reef: A spectacular site for spotting schooling fish, reef sharks, and vibrant coral gardens. Woodhouse Reef: A thrilling drift dive with sweeping currents and potential sightings of eagle rays and turtles. Each day offers 2–3 dives, with opportunities for night dives on select evenings. The dive schedule is complemented by periods of relaxation, snorkeling, and enjoying the stunning views of the Red Sea. Day 6: Return to Hurghada After breakfast, the liveaboard makes its way back to Hurghada. The last two dives may be scheduled for today, or it may be a non-diving day, allowing guests time to clean and pack their equipment. Guests can relax on deck, swap dive stories, or explore Hurghada on their own before a farewell dinner onboard. Day 7: Disembarkation (Hurghada) Guests bid farewell to the crew and disembark. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Best of Tiran::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Days 2-6: Departing & check dive. Cruising according to the planned route. Day 7: 2 dives on the last day. Return to the port. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. The best sites in the area of Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, Gubal Strait and the Strait of Tiran in the Gulf of Aqaba. (As with all circuits, order and site selection can not only be contractual; they can be varied due to the weather and/or state of the sea). A circuit that will take you to the Strait of Tiran, through the reserve of Ras Mohamed and wrecks like the mythical Thistlegorm, Rosalie Moeller... This tour will allow you to dive on steep drop-offs, reefs with fish, pelagic carangos, eagle rays, sharks... Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Brother Islands - Daedalus - Elphinstone.programme:
Program
Day 1: Check-in from 4:00 PM. Overnight on the boat. Day 2: 1st dive - Ras Disha. 2nd dive - Wreck of the Salem Express. 3rd dive - Middle Reef. Day 3: 1st dive - Big Brother South. 2nd dive - Big Brother (Numidia wreck). 3rd dive - Little Brother. Day 4: 1st dive - Daedalus North. 2nd dive - Daedalus East. 3rd dive - Daedalus South. Day 5: 1st dive - Daedalus. 2nd dive - Daedalus. 3rd dive - Daedalus West. Day 6: 1st Dive - Elphinstone North. 2nd dive - Elphinstone South. 3rd Dive - Marsa Alam Area. 4th dive - night dive. Day 7: 1st dive - Panorama Reef. 2nd dive - El Mina wreck. Day 8: Check-out from 9:00 am. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Daedalus - Rocky - Zabargad - Elphinston.programme:
Program
Day 1: Check-in day. Guests can check in from 5 pm until 3 am the following morning to get to the boat in time. Services start on day 1 after check-in, and evening dinner is included on board. The boat leaves between 9 and 10 am on day 2. Day 2: Departure for St. John’s after breakfast. Days 3–6: Up to 3 dives a day exploring the stunning reefs. Day 7: Dives are planned, but this depends on the flight schedule of the guests. The boat will be back in the afternoon. The last night will be spent at the marina, and dinner will be served on board. Day 8: Breakfast is included, and check-out is between 8 and 9 am. Guests can go straight to the airport to catch their flight. Transfers are organized by the boat. Rocky Island and Zabargad Rocky Island has become a shelter and nesting place for a large variety of birds. Zabargad, the bigger of the two islands, has quite a steep relief and is surrounded by a marvelous turquoise lagoon. During summer, it becomes a rendezvous place for turtles, where they gather to lay their eggs. The best description would be: wild landscapes and isolated sites, lost in the middle of the Red Sea. Daedalus On the northern side of Daedalus, we will make a sunrise dive. This is the most exposed side of Daedalus, with strong sea currents and the best chance of encounters with pelagic species. It is quite common to dive with schools of more than 20 hammerhead sharks. Carangidae and tunas are regularly present. We will then leave the deep zone to explore the reef wall. This exploration requires close attention, as the wall is full of holes and overhangs. Many black coral branches can be seen colonizing the reef. While ascending, don’t forget to look up: you may see barracudas nearby. Zabargad On Zabargad Island, you can still see fragments of emerald-like rocks that gave the island its fame and name. Zabargad is the Arabic name for the green-olive mineral that once filled this semi-volcanic island. The dive site is characterized by peaks, canyons, caves, and walls. You can encounter tunas, scorpionfish, leopard sharks, nurse sharks, angelfish, groupers, morays, blue dotted stingrays, and mantas. Rocky Five km south of Zabargad lies Rocky Island, near the Sudanese border. Undoubtedly, Rocky Island is one of the wildest diving sites in Egypt. Diving over the shallow platform, which shelters all kinds of marine life, leads to a wall covered with giant gorgonians, sponges, and corals. The south of the island is a meeting point for whitefin sharks, grey reef sharks, and mantas. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Day 2: Departure in the morning around 8-9 am, 2 check dives near the coast of Marsa Alam, 3rd dive or possible night dive in the area, sailing overnight to the Fury Shoal reefs. Days 3-5: Spending time at Fury's, 3-4 dives possible per day, including 1 possible night dive. Possible dive sites: Malahi, Shab Claudio, Shab Maksur, Sataya/Dolphin Reef. Day 6: Return to Port Ghalib, possibly 2 dives in Elphinstone or in the Marsa Alam area – weather dependent. Day 7: The last 2 dives in the Marsa Alam area, the last night on board. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Marine Park - Simply the Best::14.programme:
Program
DAY 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. DAY 2-13: Departing & check dive. Cruising according to the planned route. DAY 14: 2 dives on the last day. Return to the port. DAY 15: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Diving lovers will be fully satisfied from the BLUE HOLE (north of Dahab) to the extreme south (Sudan borders) on the reefs of Abu Fendira. Several stops by the most beautiful wrecks of the north of the Red Sea, Sinai cape and the wonderful Ras Mohamed National Park, coral reefs of Tiran situated at the gates of El Aqaba Gulf, the mystic Brothers Islands, Rocky, Zabargad, Elphinstone not to mention Daedalus. In brief, the cruise regroups in 12 days/14 nights, all of the most beautiful dive sites of the Red Sea. The reason why we call it “Simply The Best”. This circuit will alternate the deep falls and their schools of pelagic fishes, wreck diving and highly colored low depth reefs that will suit photography lovers. You will also discover the caves and their “cathedrals” with their magnificent underwater lighting setups, snorkeling among dolphins and of course the surprise of the uninspected rendezvous. That’s what makes, no doubt, the charm of this unique cruise. We will be pleased to make you discover different rarely wonderful dives by the Rocky Island and by the magnificent Zabargad where we spare especially for you some unforgettable surprises Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)
